images.title: 60 × 70 is 42 hundreds
images.purpose: Show that 6 tens times 7 tens makes 6 × 7 = 42 blocks of 100, so 60 × 70 = 4,200.
images.composition: An array of 6 rows of 7 blocks marked 100 on the left, with 60 = 6 tens and 70 = 7 tens marked on its sides, and the sentences 60 × 70, 6 × 7 = 42 and 42 hundreds = 4,200 on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the left, one array of exactly 42 blocks in 6 rows of 7 columns. Every block is a rounded square (corner radius 10 px), 72 by 72 px, filled teal #0072B2 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and the number 100 in white bold sans-serif (30 px) centred in it; neighbouring blocks are 8 px apart across and down. The array's top left corner is at x 100 and y 160 and it spans x 100 to 652 and y 160 to 632. Above it, a green #009E73 double headed arrow (3 px line) from x 100 to x 652 at y 130, with the label 70 = 7 tens in green bold sans-serif (34 px) centred at x 376 and y 95. At the left of it, a reddish purple #CC79A7 double headed arrow (3 px line) from y 160 to y 632 at x 72. Under the array, centred at x 376 and y 690, the label 60 = 6 tens in reddish purple bold sans-serif (34 px). At the right, left aligned at x 760, three lines in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif: 60 × 70 at y 270 (64 px), 6 × 7 = 42 at y 370 (56 px) and 42 hundreds = 4,200 at y 470 (56 px). In all there are 42 blocks, none missing, each marked 100. No other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Multiply the digits, 6 × 7 = 42, and the answer is 42 hundreds, so 60 × 70 = 4,200.
images.description: An array of 42 blocks marked 100, 6 rows of 7, beside the sentences 60 × 70, 6 × 7 = 42 and 42 hundreds = 4,200.
images.context: Concept image for Multiplying Tens, Hundreds and Thousands. It follows the idea of the multiplication pattern in your maths book (multiply the digits, then write the zeros) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 60 and 70.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student count the blocks by rows and columns and see that each block is 100. The slip to watch: writing 60 × 70 = 42 or 420 and forgetting that the answer is in hundreds.

image_decisions.why: The array of hundred blocks shows why 60 × 70 is 42 hundreds, which the rule about zeros does not.
